- **Automatic bounded lesson recall at planning time (#205)**: the orchestrator now consults past lessons before `planner` is dispatched and with no manual command — a grep-only read, first frontmatter block only, over `.context/decisions.md`, `.context/issues.md`, `.context/DESIGN-RULES.md` and the plan frontmatter under `plan/complete/`, capped at 3 completed plans, 2k tokens and ~30 lines per plan (frontmatter, Goal, Scope, lesson outcome), where a no-match read costs the grep alone, a pointer line in `.context/progress.md` names the sources and their dates (the latest dated decision supersedes), and `planner` receives the slice under Inputs Available and never re-runs it; the step never reads `.context/comprehension-log.md`, `.context/research-dataset.jsonl`, `.context/triage-dataset.jsonl` or `.context/comprehension/**`, never triggers `/recall` and never runs inside a task lifecycle, so manual `/recall` semantics are untouched. Plans gain two optional flat-scalar frontmatter keys — `tags: alpha,beta` and `outcome` — with `plan_board move --outcome` writing the lesson outcome only on promotion to `complete` and `check` staying silent when either key is absent; `scripts/plan-board.py`, `plugin/src/plan-board.ts` and the `plan_board` tool schema carry the same contract, so Python↔TypeScript parity is enforced, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` is the canonical home for the caps and the isolation rules while `README.md` only cross-links, and `tests/lesson-recall.test.ts` plus the extended board suites pin the prompt surface, the isolation sinks and the new keys.
- **Workflow intake and adaptive complexity gate (#198)**: every request is intake-checked before routing — `agents/orchestrator.md` gains a thin `## Workflow intake and adaptive complexity gate` pointer and `agents/orchestrator-quick.md` an ambiguous-request hand-back bullet, while the operational protocol lives in the on-demand `workflow-intake` skill, loaded only for an ambiguous request (goal, scope, affected files, or constraints neither stated nor inferable from the request, session memory, project profile, or repo) or a `workflow.mode` decision — a clear request under `auto` routes exactly as today, with no skill load and no announce line. The restated spec is triaged categorically: `NONE` is the existing small-task shortcut (at most one file or no plan needed → `/quick`), `LIGHT` is the bounded band between NONE and DEEP (single-concern, single-module multi-file work handled with direct delegations and no plan card), and `DEEP` is security-sensitive, cross-module, or multi-phase work (plan card through `planner`/`plan-writer`, then review and comprehension gate) — never a numeric score, and the three classes are disjoint and jointly exhaustive. `workflow.mode` in the new `templates/workflow.config.json` (`auto` by default, `full` forces the standard flow, `lite` permits the slim path only by an announced decision) makes that triage configurable at prompt level with no runtime loader; triage telemetry is opt-in and off by default (`triageTelemetry.enabled: false`), appending `TriageEventV1` rows to the untracked, append-only `.context/triage-dataset.jsonl` that is never read at bootstrap, and `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `README.md` and `/start-session` document the gate; `tests/intake-triage.test.ts` pins the restatement protocol, the disjoint class mapping, the mode vocabulary, the telemetry opt-in and the absence of the replaced clarifying-questions sentence.
- **Vendored the MIT-licensed `security-audit` skill (#197)**: `skills/security-audit/` now carries the Cloudflare security-audit skill (github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill, © 2025-2026 Cloudflare, pinned at commit `c1c8a8c`; 20 files plus `LICENSE`), `agents/security.md` gains `security-audit: allow` in its `permission.skill` map so security reviews can load the audit methodology in guidance mode, while full audit mode (writes on disk) stays out of scope for that read-only agent; `scripts/sync-assets.ts` an

- **Explicit containment for the `apply-freellmapi-profile.py` config lifecycle (#147 #148 #149 #150)**: the read, the dated `.bak-<ts>` backup copy, the terminal write and the `json.dump` payload now all consume a single `--config` path resolved and verified before any filesystem access — an empty value, a `..` segment in either separator form (`/` and `\`, mixed included) or a value that resolves outside the config root it names is refused with `ERROR: --config …, refusing: …` and exit 1, so the four Snyk sinks share one decision point instead of four; clean relative and absolute paths keep working unchanged, `--dry-run` and `--force-config` behave as before, and the documented exit codes are untouched.
- **Explicit containment for the `apply-model-preset.py` config read (#146)**: `load_config`'s `Path(args.config)` read no longer consumes the raw argv value — the path is resolved once (`abspath` + `normpath`) and contained before any filesystem access, so an empty value, a `..` segment in either separator form (`/` and `\`, mixed included) or a value that resolves outside the config root it names is refused with `error: --config …, refusing: …` and exit 1; clean relative and absolute `--config` values keep working unchanged, and `--list`, `--restore` and `--dry-run` behave exactly as before.
- **Explicit containment for the three `plan-board.py` sinks (#143 #144 #145)**: `move` and `new` no longer hand a raw `--root`-joined destination to `mkdir`/`write_text` — the source and the target are resolved (`Path.resolve`, symlinked columns included) and must stay under the resolved board root, while `--body` resolves once (`abspath` + `normpath`) and refuses an empty value, a `..` segment in either separator form (`/` and `\`, mixed included) or a path that resolves outside the parent directory it names, so an absolute `--root` and an explicit `.context/plan-body-<id>.md` body keep working exactly as before; every refusal reuses the existing `path-traversal` JSON envelope (never renamed), payload strings stay `str(root)`/`str(dst)`, and py↔TS parity is untouched because `plugin/src/plan-board.ts` is unguarded by design and its scenarios only use clean inputs.
- **Explicit containment for the two `context-budget.ts` sinks (#157 #158)**: the CLI adapter no longer hands an argv value to `readFileSync` — `--manifest` is resolved under the declared `--root`, `--config` under `--root` when relative and under the parent directory it names when absolute (the explicit operator path `loadGateConfig` uses as-is), and both are refused before any filesystem access when empty, when they carry a `..` segment in either separator form (`/` and `\`, mixed included) or when the resolved path escapes that root — so a drive-absolute second segment that `join` would not neutralize on Windows can no longer leave the tree; `--manifest -` (stdin), the report schema, the exit codes and the filesystem-free pure core are unchanged, and an absolute `--manifest` inside `--root` plus an explicit absolute `--config` keep working exactly as before.

- **Explicit containment for the two `evidence-check.ts` sinks (#155 #156)**: the CLI adapter no longer hands an argv value or a citation path to `readFileSync` — `--claims` and `--doc` are resolved under `--root` and refused before any filesystem access, as is every citation path, when the value is empty, carries a `..` segment in either separator form (`/` and `\`, mixed included) or is absolute (POSIX `/...`, drive-qualified `C:\...`, drive-relative `C:...`, UNC `\\server\share`); citations are repository-relative by contract, so an absolute `--claims`/`--doc` is refused instead of re-anchored, a value that resolves outside `--root` is refused as well, and only that validated absolute path reaches `readFileSync`, while the report schema, the exit codes and the filesystem-free pure core (`checkEvidenceClaims`/`extractCitations` behind an injected reader) are unchanged and clean relative manifests, relative citatio

v1.2.2
Patch release promoting the already-merged #172 and #171 work from Unreleased; npm publish and the Pages deploy workflow both ran green on the pushed v1.2.2 tag.
What's new
- CRG usage is mandatory when configured across the six CRG-enabled agents (#172): explorer, planner, developer-fixer, test-engineer, code-reviewer and security now treat Code Review Graph as a MUST whenever either detection signal is present (the delegation's Code Graph: present note, or code-review-graph_* tools in the native or Code Mode catalog), replacing the optional/MAY wording. The fallback stays narrow (absent, error, timeout, empty, not_ready/stale_graph → proceed with rg/read silently, never block the task), code-reviewer stays the sole refresh owner, and agents/security.md gains execute: allow so its read-only CRG tools are reachable under V2 Code Mode.
- GitHub Pages deploys on release tags and What's new comes from the changelog (#171): .github/workflows/deploy.yml now also runs on v* tag pushes, so the landing page republishes per release without a manual dispatch, and the page's What's new section is generated at build time from the released CHANGELOG.md section matching plugin/package.json's version (one card per top-level changelog bullet). Hero counts stay derived from agents/ and extras/.
Install / Upgrade
npm install -g opencode-orchestrator-kit@1.2.2
Full changelog
https://github.com/NicoGenti/opencode-orchestrator-kit/compare/v1.2.1...v1.2.2

## What's Changed
- Fix: agent prompts no longer silently disable Code Review Graph under V2 Code Mode (#167). The six CRG-enabled agent prompts now use the two-signal detection rule (delegation note or `code-review-graph_*` tools in the native list or the Code Mode catalog inside `execute`), docs/CONFIGURATION.md gains the "Code Review Graph (CRG) under V2 Code Mode" setup section, and the profiler's CRG reference is fixed.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NicoGenti/opencode-orchestrator-kit/compare/v1.2.0...v1.2.1

## Highlights

- Include the canonical project README in the npm package as a generated `plugin/README.md`.
- Add comprehension-coach evidence modes and actionable `NEEDS_REVIEW` recovery guidance (#137, #141).
- Add path-traversal guards to Python helper scripts (#128–#135).
- Add deterministic context-budget and evidence-check gates (#151).
- Document cache configuration, session reuse, and cache-aware prompt design (#119, #120).
- Add optional, read-only Code Review Graph support for implementation, test selection, and planning, with seven benchmark metrics (#153).

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `bun run sync-assets --check` passed.
- `bun test`: 1,200 passed, 30 failed. The clean baseline had 1,197 passed and 31 failed; the release failure set is a subset, with no release-only failures.
- `bun run format:check` reported 120 warnings versus 121 on the clean baseline; the release set is a subset.
- The npm package contains 46 files, and its README matches the root README byte-for-byte.
- Code review approved with no blocking findings.

The release workflow is configured to publish to npm on pushed `v*` tags; check its run for publication status.
